sources.title: GNWT, A Dene Way of Life: Grade Four Social Studies
sources.note: Official teaching resource, especially PDF pages 21 to 22, distinguishes Dene regional groups, territories, dialects, and the wider Denendeh concept.

sources.title: Dene Nation, Statement of Traditional Dene Values and Principles
sources.note: One-page Dene statement on sharing, care, elders, children, gender, medicine people, land, law, and group decisions.

sources.title: Athabasca Nuhenene, People
sources.note: Athabasca Denesuline account of identity, elders, youth, culture camps, stewardship, communities, and movement beyond imposed borders.

sources.title: Athabasca Nuhenene, Land
sources.note: Athabasca Denesuline account of Nuhenene, language-land ties, animals, fish, trees, plants, waters, and summer family gatherings.

sources.title: Athabasca Nuhenene, Caribou
sources.note: Community account of caribou as cultural keystone, whole-animal use, teaching, herd movement, respect, and stewardship.

sources.title: Athabasca Chipewyan First Nation, Language Revitalization
sources.note: First Nation page for videos, word resources, and the first Fort Chipewyan k’aitele-dialect Denesuline reader.

sources.title: GNWT, Indigenous Languages Conversations: Dene Suline
sources.note: Official one-page teaching sheet containing the exact sample, pronunciation guide, response, name question, and thanks.

sources.title: GNWT, List of Specialized Letters and Accents
sources.note: Official orthography table for glottal stop, barred l, diaeresis, acute tone, ogonek nasalization, and dotless i.

sources.title: GNWT, Preferred Spellings of Indigenous Language Names and Speakers
sources.note: Official table gives Dene Suline as the preferred spelling for both language and people.

sources.title: GNWT, Dene Kede and Inuuqatigiit
sources.note: Official curriculum overview connects language, culture, lifelong learning, land, spiritual world, self, people, and capable citizenship.

sources.title: GNWT, Dene Kede K-6 Teacher Resource Manual
sources.note: Community-consulted manual, especially PDF pages 6 and 9 to 11, on elders, local programs, land, language, and relationships.

sources.title: Parlee, Manseau, and Łutsël K’é Dene First Nation, Using Traditional Knowledge to Adapt to Ecological Change: Denésoliné Monitoring of Caribou Movements
sources.note: Community-reviewed Arctic article, journal pages 29 to 35, on family camps, water crossings, knowledge, sharing, women, and care.

sources.title: Carleton University Rangifer Central, Dene Artifact Descriptions
sources.note: Museum-linked inventory of Chipewyan and Late Taltheilei tools, materials, containers, clothing-work implements, and seasonal variation.

sources.title: Carleton University Rangifer Central, Taltheilei
sources.note: Archaeological synthesis of early, middle, and late Taltheilei chronology, ranges, sites, herd-following, tools, and attribution.

sources.title: Marles, The Ethnobotany of the Chipewyan of Northern Saskatchewan
sources.note: University thesis abstract for 1980 to 1982 fieldwork, 25 elders, 72 plant species, foods, medicines, materials, and personal variation.

sources.title: VanStone, The Snowdrift Chipewyan
sources.note: 1960 to 1962 participant-observation report, especially PDF pages 42 to 43 and 92 to 93, on parenting, toilets, outhouses, and sanitation.

sources.title: Athabasca Chipewyan First Nation, Remembering Our Relations
sources.note: Community-owned oral-history project on Dene homelands, Wood Buffalo park displacement, family separation, rights, healing, and archives.

sources.title: Parks Canada and partners, Thaidene Nene Relationship Plan
sources.note: Co-authored plan defines Dene Yati names, dialect variation, land of the ancestors, Dene knowledge, guardianship, and future generations.

sources.title: University of Saskatchewan, Denesuline in the Indigenous Saskatchewan Encyclopedia
sources.note: University reference distinguishes Athabasca and Churchill regions, communities, seasonal caribou, dialect variation, gatherings, and feasts.

sources.title: Parks Canada, Thanadelthur National Historic Person
sources.note: Official commemoration dates Thanadelthur’s 1715 to 1716 interpreting and peacemaking, far later than the atlas interval.

sources.title: GNWT, Dene Suline greetings PDF
sources.note: Direct one-page PDF for the exact written forms, pronunciation guides, and translations of hello, good morning, name, and thanks.

sources.title: Dene Nation, Dene National Assemblies
sources.note: Community organization describes annual assemblies in communities across five regions of Denendeh, with people traveling from 30 Dene communities.

sources.title: Athabasca Nuhenene homepage
sources.note: Community homepage identifies Nuhenene as Athabasca Denesuline territory, elders as knowledge keepers, caribou as keystone, and movement beyond borders.

sources.title: Lutsel K’e Dene First Nation, Land of the Ancestors
sources.note: Community site identifies Thaidene Nene as Lutsel K’e Dene homeland and connects Dene law, ancestors, forest, tundra, water, culture, and future care.

sources.title: Lutsel K’e Dene First Nation, Etthen (Caribou)
sources.note: Community page connects caribou with physical, cultural, linguistic, emotional, and spiritual life, Dene law, teaching, monitoring, and respectful hunting.

sources.title: Lutsel K’e Dene First Nation, Our Dene Laws
sources.note: Community page explains three place-based laws, elder mapping, member understanding, a recorded 2018 vote, and responsibilities in Thaidene Nene.

sources.title: Lutsel K’e Dene First Nation, Artillery Lake
sources.note: Community page documents names, stories, fall family gathering, crossings, tools, sharing, drying, caching, camp placement, and remembered childhood.

sources.title: Parks Canada, Dene Relations with Wood Buffalo National Park, 1922-2001
sources.note: Government historical report on Dene homelands, displacement, park regulation, treaty rights, harvesting, and twentieth-century change.

sources.title: Lutsel K’e Dene First Nation, Lady of the Falls
sources.note: Community-shared story locates creation history, hunger, sharing, care, prayer, place-based law, watershed protection, and continuing responsibility.
